authTierRationale: The API-token mode needs only two self-serve values a Zendesk admin can generate in the account UI (their own login email plus an API token); the connector base64-encodes "{email}/token:{api_token}" into an HTTP Basic Authorization header, so nothing has to be registered anywhere. That is T1_SIMPLE and it is the easiest mode offered. The alternative OAuth mode is T2_BYO_APP standalone: the config schema accepts a bare `access_token` but obtaining one requires a registered Zendesk OAuth client, and the client_id/client_secret fields are populated by Estuary's hosted control plane via complete_oauth_server_output_specification rather than by the user. It is not T3 - Zendesk OAuth tokens here are long-lived and no refresh_token is stored or exchanged anywhere in the connector.

unionMisfits.description: This is a legacy Airbyte-derived connector: the stream logic subclasses airbyte_cdk HttpStream and is wrapped by estuary_cdk.shim_airbyte_cdk.CaptureShim. It does NOT use the estuary-cdk native HTTPMixin/TokenSource machinery, so none of the CDK's credential or pagination abstractions apply. The successor connector source-zendesk-support-native is a different implementation of the same API.

The page-numbered paginator is not driven by responses at all. Before any page is fetched the connector GETs `{path}/count.json`, divides the returned count by page_size=100, and fires every page 1..N concurrently through a requests-futures session. There is no sequential next-page step and no termination signal from the data responses; `next_page_token` is hard-coded to None. `page_size` is used only client-side to compute N - it is never sent as a query parameter, so the page count silently depends on the API's own default page size matching 100.

sla_policies, custom_roles, schedules, account_attributes, attribute_definitions, ticket_forms and UserSettingsStream override request_params to return {} while INHERITING a next_page_token that still reads meta.after_cursor/meta.has_more. The token is computed and then discarded, so pagination is effectively disabled rather than absent - recorded here as type "none". If any of these endpoints ever returns meta.has_more=true the Airbyte read loop would re-issue the identical first-page request forever, which is the classic silent-truncation/loop failure. Recorded as `none` because that is the observable wire behaviour.

recordsPath is not a plain JSON pointer. ticket_comments reads `ticket_events[]`, then descends into each record's `child_events[]` and keeps only entries whose event_type == "Comment", copying via_reference_id/ticket_id/timestamp down from the parent event. ticket_metrics reads `tickets[]` (sideloaded with include=metric_sets) and emits each ticket's `metric_set` object, skipping tickets that have none. The extracted document is therefore a different entity than the listed one.

audit_logs ignores start_time entirely and instead sends the SAME query parameter name twice as an array: filter[created_at][]=<lower bound>&filter[created_at][]=<upper bound>, with sort=created_at to force ascending order. The upper bound is now-30s to avoid dropping records sharing the boundary timestamp. `incrementalParam` has no slot for a two-sided window.

ticket_audits is a child stream whose own cursor is borrowed from its parent. It instantiates Tickets with is_parent=True; the parent's cursor-export sweep yields a synthetic {'cursor': ...} sentinel record interleaved just before the last real record of each response, and the child intercepts that sentinel to advance its own after_cursor state instead of emitting it. The per-request pull shape (tickets/{id}/audits, meta cursor paging) is unrelated to the cursor that is checkpointed.

The stream list is static, but three entries are gated at runtime: ticket_forms, account_attributes and attribute_definitions are appended only if a probe read of ticket_forms returns at least one record, because those endpoints exist only on Enterprise plans and Zendesk exposes no plan API. So a discover call on a non-Enterprise account returns 24 streams and on Enterprise 27 - the list is shipped, but conditionally pruned. That is neither `static` nor `discovered` as the schema means them.

The Basic username is derived, not supplied: the connector appends the literal "/token" to the user's email before base64-encoding, and then sends the result through a TokenAuthenticator with auth_method="Basic" rather than through requests' native basic auth. A consumer that naively base64s email:token will get 401s.

The connector has no schedule of its own. estuary_cdk's shim drives one pass of the Airbyte `read()` generator per task invocation and returns when task.stopping is set; sweep cadence is entirely a property of the Flow runtime, not of this code. `null` here means "externally driven", which is different from "we looked and could not tell".

A connector-wide kill switch for pagination, not a normal setting: when true every stream's next_page_token short-circuits to None, so each sweep reads exactly one page. It silently truncates output rather than failing, and there is no per-stream override.

abstained.streams[26].pull.incremental.incremental: No incremental query parameter is sent at all; the endpoint is read in full each sweep and records are filtered client-side in BaseSourceZendeskSupportStream.parse_response by comparing updated_at against the checkpointed cursor (streams.py 194-201).
abstained.execution.defaultSchedule: The connector performs one Airbyte read() pass per invocation and contains no sleep/interval/cron logic; the shim only yields to the event loop (asyncio.sleep(0)) and returns on task.stopping. Sweep cadence is set by the Flow runtime outside this repository directory, so no interval could be recovered.
abstained.execution.continuity: mode is "poll" over a stateless REST API. No server-side artifact is created on the customer's Zendesk account and nothing accrues while we are stopped. The only pause-sensitive value is the Zendesk cursor-export `after_cursor`; the connector never handles a cursor-expiry error path, so no resume window could be established from the source.
abstained.streams[*].writeDisposition: The connector itself never declares a write disposition. The shim always sets Airbyte destination_sync_mode="append" and stamps _meta.op="u", and every stream here has a source-defined key (/id, /name, /subject), so the effective behaviour in Flow is keyed last-write-wins. "merge" is recorded on that basis and is an inference about the runtime, not a value read out of this connector.
abstained.streams[*].schedules: No per-binding schedule exists; the resource config carries only stream/syncMode/namespace/cursorField.
abstained.streams[macros|ticket_fields].pull.incre: request_params sets start_time for the page requests, but the Zendesk /macros and /ticket_fields list endpoints are not documented as time-filterable and the connector's own count call drops the parameter, so it could not be confirmed that the parameter has any effect.
